Resolves #19444

The lost-context test took `drawn` from the first read with the scene's 240 nodes. On a loaded runner that read can come before the first resize report, so it compared the correctly restored 2000×1288 buffer against the canvas default 300×150. That happened in 2 of the last 11 `dev` e2e runs. One helper, `sizedSceneDrawn()`, now waits for the scene drawn into a buffer of the canvas's CSS size × 2, and both tests take `drawn` from it. Test 1 keeps its frame settle for the idle second. No engine change: the restore was already right.

Evidence: local e2e (`playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, 2 tests × 3 serial repeats, 6/6 passed) → CI's E2E engine tier runs the same spec. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `GraphScene.spec.mjs` › both tests call `sizedSceneDrawn()`, whose predicate requires the counts and `canvas` equal to the box × 2 |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `GraphScene.spec.mjs` › "a lost context comes back with its scene, and a resize keeps it" compares the restore against that sized snapshot |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: `npx playwright test test/playwright/e2e/rendering/GraphScene.spec.mjs -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --repeat-each=3 --workers=1` → 6 passed (19.1s) at `aeca7af1a8` |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive.

## Test Evidence
The two `dev` reds (runs 37457558206 and 37615497209) failed on this test's restore assertion: expected `[300,150]`, received `[2000,1288]`. The local runs above pass at the fixed head. I did not try to reproduce the timing under load.
